competitive_landscape: There is no scheduled passenger ferry on the UAE east coast - everything moves by road over the Hajar mountains, and transfers to the offshore anchorage run on conventional diesel launches. The pain is concrete: a slow, winding mountain drive to reach the Indian Ocean side, no premium or on-demand water option, and a busy ship-services economy still served by noisy boats. That undifferentiated status quo is precisely the opening.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The whole east-coast chain - Fujairah, Khorfakkan, Al Aqah, Dibba - sits well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, with the calm, sheltered Gulf-of-Oman bays ideal for multi-rotation days and crew-transfer runs to the offshore anchorage on a single charge.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Opens the long Indian Ocean corridor - down the Oman coast to Sohar and Muscat, and around the Musandam peninsula into the Arabian Gulf - as single hybrid legs with no charging-infrastructure dependency (diesel refuel + near-silent electric on approach).

precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that an all-electric foiling network scales across a dispersed island/coastal market - the playbook to replicate on the UAE east coast.

regulatory_note: Operates under the Port of Fujairah authority and the UAE Federal Transport Authority - Land & Maritime. A clean, all-electric tier aligns with UAE Net Zero 2050 and gives the world's second-largest bunkering hub a visible decarbonisation story for its own in-water services.
seasonality: The Gulf of Oman is generally calm and far better sheltered than the open Arabian Sea; summer (Jun-Sep) brings heat and occasional swell, and the broader Indian Ocean monsoon can push surf onto exposed beaches. Foiling flies above the chop, so the ride stays smooth in conditions that slow and pound planing boats.

summary: Fujairah is the only emirate fully on the Gulf of Oman / Indian Ocean side of the Hajar mountains, which is exactly why it is so hard to reach by land: Dubai is a 1.5-2 hour mountain drive away. Yet its calm coastal water connects a string of resorts and dive sites - Le Meridien Al Aqah, Snoopy Island, Khorfakkan, Dibba - in minutes by sea, and the world's second-largest bunkering hub sits just offshore with thousands of ships at anchor. The east coast is an unmodernised marine surface waiting for a premium, all-electric water tier.
tagline: The UAE's Indian Ocean coast — mountains meeting the sea, and one of the busiest anchorages on earth offshore.

use_cases.body: Smooth, fast foiling along the mountain-to-sea coast - Fujairah town, Khorfakkan, Le Meridien Al Aqah / Snoopy Island, Dibba - turning a chain of winding coastal-road drives into single short hops, comfortable in the Gulf-of-Oman swell that pounds conventional craft.
